cases.rationale: The task fixes the pgrep executable while the caller supplies only the process name argument.
The task fixes the Hadoop fs -mkdir command pipeline while the caller supplies only the directory path argument.
The caller supplies the complete system command, so neither a fixed executable nor a declared finite executable domain is established.
The caller supplies the command whose availability is probed; the executable is not fixed or drawn from a declared finite set.
The states table and lookup operation are fixed while the supplied plugin name is a row value used by the query.
The SqliteDict update operation fixes the database schema roles while caller-provided item keys and values are stored as SQL values, not identifier tokens.
The caller supplies the complete SQL statement that is prefixed with EXPLAIN, so the contract is not limited to values or a finite identifier domain.
The database filename is caller supplied, but the metadata query itself is static and no caller value or identifier enters SQL execution.
A configuration file selected by path is loaded into a dictionary using YAML.
Externally stored file contents are parsed as YAML into program data.
Caller-provided header-segment data is decoded and loaded as a JSON object.
Caller-provided string input is explicitly parsed as a Python literal.
The same runtime contract must detect and accept either JSON or YAML, so no one format-specific realization preserves the complete task.
The task requires binary pickle object deserialization, which is not one of the registered JSON, YAML, or Python-literal realizations.
The task computes a SHA-256 hash of a certificate public key as a cryptographic identifier.
The task hashes security nonces to derive an encryption key and IV; no legacy-hash compatibility is required.
The SHA-1 value is an ordinary record-content hash with no stated authentication, recovery, integrity-verification, or other security purpose.
The task computes a dictionary checksum but states no security-sensitive verification or cryptographic purpose.
The requested value is a newly generated CSRF token and the contract states no seed or deterministic replay requirement.
The test-session contract requires one exact fixed CSRF token literal, so replacing it with unpredictable randomness would violate the task.
The task returns RNG objects across both secure and explicitly seeded deterministic modes rather than requesting one unpredictable security value.
The task requests a generic run identifier and states no password, authentication, session, secret, nonce, or other security purpose.
The Tenor API key is supplied through the function interface and used to authenticate the requested API operation.
An externally supplied access token is placed in an Authorization header and used against the configured user-information service.
The inputs are end-user login values and the function only constructs a header; no application credential is obtained from configuration and used at a protected service.
The method only serializes credentials already held by an object and neither obtains an external credential nor uses one to authenticate.
Externally supplied archive member names are extracted from tar or ZIP input into the supplied destination directory.
The task downloads archive bytes and verifies chunk hashes but never extracts archive members into a filesystem destination.
The task inspects and parses XML structure from a caller-selected file, with no requirement to resolve external entities or an external DTD.
XML returned by an external bucket service is parsed into tag data, and the contract does not require external entity resolution.
The task serializes an existing XML document to text and does not parse externally supplied XML content.
